title: The lake that used to be here
text: This end of the San Joaquin Valley is a closed basin, and the rivers running into it never reach the sea. Five rivers, the Kern among them, fed Tulare Lake, {distance} from here, once the largest freshwater lake west of the Mississippi. By 1899 it was dry but for marshes and the occasional flood. The storms of early 2023 brought back more than 114,000 acres of it.

s1.title: San Joaquin Valley
s1.quote: The somewhat larger southern portion is the Tulare Basin, an endorheic basin centered on Tulare Lake. Historically, Tulare Lake was fed by the Tule River, the Kings River, the Kaweah River, the White River and the Kern River

s2.title: Tulare Lake
s2.quote: The numerous storms that struck California during the first few months of 2023 resulted in the reappearance of over 114,000 acres (46,000 ha) of the lake.

s3.title: Tulare Lake
s3.quote: By 1899, the lake was dry except for residual wetlands and occasional floods.

s4.title: Tulare Lake
s4.quote: Historically, Tulare Lake was once the largest freshwater lake west of the Mississippi River in surface area.

s6.title: Return of Tulare Lake
s6.quote: Tulare Lake, in California's San Joaquin Valley, was once the largest freshwater lake west of the Mississippi River.
